Definition: {Midjan, a son of Abraham; also his country and (collectively) his descendants}
BiblicalUsage: Middin is named once, in the list of the wilderness cities of Judah: Beth-arabah, Middin and Secacah. It is a town in the wilderness, and its name is the whole of what Scripture tells us.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that even a wilderness town in a list is part of the inheritance: Judah's border ran through Middin, and God gave His people the wilderness too.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
